subject: Follow-up: AP constraints & procurement timeline (Stellarus)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@stellarus.com>, Amanda Ruiz <amanda.ruiz@stellarus.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: AP constraints & procurement timeline (Stellarus)

Hi Jordan / Amanda —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement has what they need to decide between PO vs card for the pilot: 

Highlights from the call:
- Procurement preference: prefer PO for production purchases, require vendor registration in their portal and standard onboarding docs (W-9, bank ACH, COI).
- AP timing: typical PO creation lead time is 3–6 weeks once vendor is onboarded; invoice/ACH processing is Net 30 or Net 60 depending on contract.
- Card policy: corporate cards can be used for pilot purchases but limits apply — current cap is $5,000 per vendor without extra approvals.
- Marketplace option: you mentioned AWS Marketplace as a faster procurement path if they prefer a marketplace billing model.

Attached: onboarding_requirements_v2.pdf — a short checklist of documents procurement usually asks for.

Proposed next steps (owners):
1) Jordan/Amanda: confirm whether pilot budget will be on card or PO (date: by EOD Wed).
2) Marcus: if card pilot, share a pricing estimate and sample invoice for internal approvals (I'll attach that once you confirm).
3) Laura/Evelyn: if PO path, we'll start the vendor onboarding packet and share the W-9 + ACH template for your vendor portal.

If it helps, we can propose a hybrid: card for the first small pilot to unblock engineering, then PO for sustained usage after procurement onboarding completes.

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick call with procurement if useful.

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer

From: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@stellarus.com>

Cc: Amanda Ruiz <amanda.ruiz@stellarus.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: AP constraints & procurement timeline (Stellarus)

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. A few clarifications from AP/procurement side: 

- Vendor onboarding: we require a completed vendor packet (W-9, bank ACH form, certificate of insurance). Vendor must be created in our vendor portal before we issue a PO. Portal link: https://www.stellarus.com/vendor-portal (will need company tax info).
- Card limits: our standard card policy limits single-vendor charges without program manager approval to $5k. For anything above that we need a PO or an exception approved by finance.
- Timing: vendor creation usually takes 2–3 business days once packet is submitted, PO issuance then adds ~2–3 weeks depending on workload. Overall 3–4 weeks if everything is in order.

For the pilot, we can do a card-backed purchase if the initial scope is <$5k. If you can provide a sample invoice and SOW skeleton we can route to the PM for quick approval.

I've attached the vendor packet checklist we use internally (vendor_packet_required.xlsx).

Jordan
Director, Procurement
Stellarus, Inc.
jordan.cole@stellarus.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: AP constraints & procurement timeline (Stellarus)

Jordan — great, thanks for the details and the packet. Quick proposal based on what you shared: 

Option A — Fast pilot (recommended if technical unblock is priority):
- Use corporate card for initial pilot (<= $5k). Redwood will provide a sample invoice and a short SOW. Pilot can start within days once card approval is done.

Option B — PO + vendor onboarding (recommended for production or >$5k spend):
- We complete the vendor packet now. Expect vendor creation in 2–3 business days once we return W-9/ACH/COI; PO issuance then ~2–3 weeks, so 3–5 weeks total.

Marketplace (AWS) alternative:
- If Stellarus prefers AWS Marketplace billing, we can initiate marketplace onboarding; that can shorten procurement friction in some orgs but requires a contract addendum and marketplace listing steps.

Next actions I can take this week:
- Send a 1-page SOW + sample invoice and the pricing estimate (attached: pricing_estimate_stellarus.xlsx).
- Start vendor packet paperwork if you confirm PO route and share the vendor contact email for portal registration.

If you'd like, I can draft a short note for your PM/finance describing the pilot scope and cost to accelerate card approval.

Best,
Marcus
--
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Jordan — adding the procurement checklist and a suggested timeline from our side to make the PO path straightforward: 

Procurement checklist (we will provide):
- Completed W-9 (signed)
- Bank ACH form (for vendor setup)
- Certificate of Insurance (general liability)
- Vendor legal name + remit address + tax ID
- Sample invoice template for your AP team

Suggested timeline if PO path chosen:
- Day 0–2: Redwood returns completed W-9 + ACH + COI to your portal contact.
- Day 3–7: Vendor creation in portal and internal checks.
- Week 2–3: PO issuance and initial invoice submission.

If you need an accelerated PO, please identify the procurement contact (and any internal approvers) and we can coordinate a short exception request. For the pilot card flow, Marcus's SOW + sample invoice should be sufficient for your PM to approve.

DocuSign SOW template: https://redwood.com/sow-template (I can pre-fill if you send the pilot budget & billing contact).

Laura Bennett
